<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 13d52947d81aca235133ee9619d80723a7c63348` → `packageMentionDocs`.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1ea01b6649c1b274734643bd918b510394beeaab`

Independent contract review of PR #19347 against card #19064 and the repository. Reading taken 2026-09-20T13:20Z. Baselines pinned by sha and compared by sha, never by a ref name: head `1ea01b6649` (one commit over merge-base `74fb2f7a80`), today's `main` read as `2277d1fcd1`. The subject file's blob is `952315ff14` at BOTH `74fb2f7a80` and `2277d1fcd1`, and `21d35a8b8d` at head, so for this file "the PR's base" and "today's tree" are one reading. Evidence was the card body and its comments, the PR, and the repository; the dispatch order, the dev report and the triage/unlock notes were read and NOT adopted — every number below was re-taken in this review's own SHA-pinned worktrees, and the `--pair 19347` predicate was run before this record existed (exit 4 on C6 alone: no `## Contract review` on this head — the row this comment exists to close).

### ① Derived judgments

**The defect is real on today's tree — re-measured, not inherited.** `git grep -n -E 'stack\.objects|manifest\.objects' 2277d1fcd1 -- packages/lint/src/validate-translation-references.ts` prints exactly two lines: `:752` (docblock prose) and `:851 for (const obj of recordsOf(stack.objects)) {` — the OBJECT rung's only universe source; `manifest.objects` is absent (the query asks for both tokens, so the absence is a reading). Lit control, same query form, same corpus: `git grep -n 'artifactProvidedObjectNames' 2277d1fcd1 -- packages/lint/src/` prints `validate-object-references.ts:163` (definition), `validate-object-references.ts:210` (its fold into `resolvable`) and `validate-translation-references.ts:692` (docblock) — the instrument lights where the token exists. Every other `recordsOf(stack.X)` in the rule on `main` reads a top-level collection only (`:938 views`, `:944 pages`, `:964 actions`, `:995 apps`, `:1050 dashboards`, `:1081 flows`); `stack.packages` is read at `:732` and `:827`, for the two contribution carriers only.

**The docblock half, read exactly — the card over-reads it, and the defect does not need it.** The `:692` claim sits in `contributedNavItemsByApp`'s docblock (`:686-:701`: "Contributions reach a stack in hand in exactly two shapes… `packages[].manifest.…` … Read with the same reach `validateObjectReferences`' `artifactProvidedObjectNames` uses (#16611), because it answers the same question: what does THIS ARTIFACT provide"). That is a reach declared for the CONTRIBUTION carriers. The file HEADER's ladder on `main` says `:112 1. own object` and its contributed-surfaces table (`:133-:135`) lists `manifest.navigationContributions` and `objectExtensions[]` only — no artifact reach for the object rung is declared there. So "the declaration and the implementation disagree inside one file" is a stretch; what the file declared was a reach for a different rung. The defect stands on its own two legs regardless: (i) the measured false orphan below, and (ii) the RULED resolution context `packageBodyAsStack` documents (`packages/cli/src/utils/artifact-packages.ts:181`, header: the per-package stack is handed the artifact's own `packages[]` as RESOLUTION CONTEXT, "it changes what a rule can RESOLVE, never what it JUDGES", and "the consuming rule owns which of an entry's contents are resolution context") — the same carrier and entry shape (`packages[].manifest.objects`, ADR-0130 D4) `artifactProvidedObjectNames` reads.

**The diff closes exactly that gap and invents no new reach.** `artifactProvidedObjects` reads `recordsOf(stack.packages)` → `entry.manifest` (`isRec` guard) → `recordsOf(body.objects)` and nothing else — the same walk as `artifactProvidedObjectNames` (its `!body || typeof body !== 'object' || Array.isArray(body)` guard is `isRec` spelled out). The one difference is the return (records, not names), judged in ③. The test helper `asPerPackageLeg` builds `{ ...body, manifest: body, packages: entries }`, which is byte-for-byte what `packageBodyAsStack` returns, and `artifactPackages` (`:113-:128`) reads entries as `entry.manifest`, so the pins model the real leg.

**Diagnostic re-run on the BASE blob (`952315ff14`), through `packageBodyAsStack`'s shape, in this review's own probe:** `core` declares `crm_account`, `orders` translates it → 1 `error`, `translations[0]["zh-CN"].objects.crm_account`, message "Translations are keyed to "crm_account", which no object in this stack defines…", hint "Rename the key to the object it was written for, drop it, or ignore this if the object is contributed by another installed package. Defined objects: crm_order." The same leg with the typo `crm_acount` → 1 `error`, identical message and hint but for the name and a `Did you mean "crm_account"?` suffix. ⇒ a legitimate sibling reference and a typo were indistinguishable at `error`, and the run fails on the remedy that deletes a translation the runtime honours (`packages/core/src/fallbacks/memory-i18n.ts:182-189`: `loadTranslations` deep-merges every bundle into ONE map per locale, package-agnostic — structural reading, not a booted composition). On the HEAD blob (`21d35a8b8d`) the sibling case prints 0 findings.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no` is right, and `@objectstack/lint: patch` matches it. Re-derived from the diff, not the changeset: **no published payload gains a key** — `TranslationRefFinding` is untouched; what moves is the VALUE of a hint string (`Defined objects:` now enumerates artifact-provided names on the per-package leg, e.g. `crm_account, crm_order` instead of `crm_order`). **No export moves** — the five `export` lines of the module are identical between `74fb2f7a80` and head (`TRANSLATION_TARGET_UNKNOWN`, `TRANSLATION_OPTION_KEY_UNKNOWN`, `TranslationRefSeverity`, `TranslationRefFinding`, `validateTranslationReferences`); `artifactProvidedObjects` and `collectObjectRecord` are module-private; `packages/lint/src/index.ts:676-685` re-exports the same names. **Accept set**: no spec schema is in the file list (3 files: the changeset, the rule, its test); the rule's false-positive set on the per-package leg narrows, so what `os build` accepts there widens to what the union leg and the ruled `packageBodyAsStack` context already accept — a pull-back to the declared contract, not a widening of it. Changeset gates re-run at head: `check-adr-0087-registration` 0, `check-changeset-no-major` 0, `check-empty-changeset` 0.

One carrier-discipline note for the PM, not a defect in the diff: `references/contract-review.md` asks a `Clause-②: no` that deletes a false rejection to carry a `Contract-text:` line citing the published text it rests on, on both carriers; neither the claim comment nor the PR body carries one, and none of the three checkers reads that key (0 hits in `check-clause2-carriers.mjs`, `check-widening-tells.mjs`, `dispatch-gates.mjs`). The text it would cite is `artifact-packages.ts:181`'s ruled context (director seat, decision batch #86) plus ADR-0130 D4 — recorded here so the claim can be completed without re-deriving it.

### ③ Boundary flags

**False negatives — judged by measurement in BOTH directions, on head `21d35a8b8d`, per-package leg unless stated (probe paths printed):**
- a name NO package declares, `crm_acount` → 1 `error` at `…objects.crm_acount`, hint `Defined objects: crm_account, crm_order.` — still caught, and the remedy now names the artifact.
- a field typo UNDER the sibling's object, `industri` → 1 `error` at `…objects.crm_account.fields.industri`, `Declared fields: industry, name.` — the subtree stays judged (this is what separates the fix from a rung-2b skip).
- UNION leg of a two-package artifact (flattened top level + `packages[]`): `crm_account` resolves, `crm_acount` → 1 `error` — the fold is a no-op on names already present, and the union leg's verdict is unchanged.
- single-`defineStack` shape (no `packages[]`) → `crm_account` still 1 `error`; a segment-reference sibling entry (`{ ref, integrity }`) → still 1 `error`, `Defined objects: crm_order.` — the widening is not a path.
- `objectExtensions[]` aimed at the SIBLING's object: injected `sla_tier` resolves, undeclared `zzz_gone` → 1 `error`, `Declared fields: industry, name, sla_tier.` On the BASE blob this same bundle prints **0 findings** — i.e. the base carried a false NEGATIVE here (rung 2b skipped the whole subtree because the target had no facts), which the record fold closes as a side effect. Named so nobody reads it as a regression.
- precedence, fields: own `crm_account.industry` (options `retail`) beside sibling's (options `tech`) → bundle option `tech` reported as `translation-option-key-unknown` (`Declared values: retail.`), `retail` silent — the stack in hand keeps the slot, as the PR says. Precedence, actions (`_actions`): own `ship` (params `eta`) keeps the slot — sibling-only param `carrier` → 1 `error`, `Declared params: eta.`; a sibling-only action `ship2` resolves and its undeclared param `zzz` → 1 `error`. Both value-carrying maps behave alike; the four name Sets (views, sections, tabs, validations) are unions, where a collision cannot change a verdict.

**Ablations — re-run here from the committed head in a separate worktree, mutation and restore proven by blob hash (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`), reds listed BY NAME:**
- **A1 — the fold's effect removed** (`collectObjectRecord(obj, { ownDeclaration: false });` → `void obj;`; anchor x1→x0, blob `21d35a8b8de4` → `115e6642cdd5`): `5 failed | 100 passed (105)`, exit 1 — `accepts the object key when a sibling package of the same artifact declares it`, `judges the subtree against the SIBLING's declaration — its field, option and rule keys resolve`, `NON-DEGENERACY — a name NO package of the artifact declares still errors` (its hint pin: the remedy must enumerate the artifact's objects), `NON-DEGENERACY — a field the sibling does not declare is still an error under the resolved object`, `separates the two directions on ONE bundle — the sibling key is silent, the typo is not`. Restored: blob == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- **A2 — a NAME-ONLY fold, the design the PR argues against** (same anchor → `factsFor(String(obj.name));`; blob → `a9913ee08921`): `3 failed | 102 passed (105)`, exit 1 — `judges the subtree against the SIBLING's declaration…`, `NON-DEGENERACY — a field the sibling does not declare…`, `separates the two directions on ONE bundle…`; `accepts the object key…` stays GREEN under this mutation, exactly as a name-only fold would behave. ⇒ the record-vs-name distinction is pinned by three named cases, not by the acceptance. Restored as above.
- **A3 — the field-precedence guard removed** (`if (!ownDeclaration && facts.fields.has(fieldName)) continue;` → `void ownDeclaration;`; blob → `f84a3b3af6d4`): `1 failed | 104 passed (105)`, exit 1 — `keeps the stack's OWN declaration when a sibling declares the same object name`. Restored as above; final `git status --porcelain` empty.
- Lit control for all three: the unmutated head runs the same file 105/105, exit 0 (above).

**Test-first red re-taken:** the head's test file against the BASE blob (`952315ff14`, restored into the tree only, blob verified) prints `5 failed | 100 passed (105)`, exit 1 — the same five names as A1, the first of them failing on the card's diagnostic verbatim; then `git checkout HEAD -- …` brought the blob back to `21d35a8b8d`. Two more base-vs-head readings from the probe: the field typo `industri` under the sibling's object is masked on base by the object-level error and surfaces on head at `…crm_account.fields.industri`; a sibling-only action `ship2` is reported on base at the action level and on head at its undeclared param `…ship2.params.zzz` — a genuine typo still yields an `error` on both sides, at the more precise address on head.

**Design — the record-vs-name argument is true on the code.** Under the object branch the only readers of a stored record are `facts.fields.get(fieldName)` → `checkOptionKeys({ field })` (`:1292-:1316`, which reads the field's `options`) and `facts.actions.get(actionName)` → `checkActionParams({ action })` (`:1406-:1426`, which reads the action's `params`); views/sections/tabs/validations are name Sets. A name-only fold (A2 above) creates the object with empty facts, so every field key under a sibling's object becomes an orphan — the same false positive one level down, exactly as the PR argues. The collision rule is confined to the two value maps (`if (!ownDeclaration && facts.X.has(name)) continue;`), the own-declaration loop runs first, and the package's own entry in `packages[]` re-walks the own objects under `ownDeclaration: false`, which is a no-op on the maps (already `has`) and idempotent on the Sets. No `stack.manifest.objects` form is read — `objects` is a stack collection, so the single-stack shape cannot pick up a second source.

**Reach — no other rung or rule changes.** `universe.objects` is read at `:1248` (the object branch), `:1277`, `:1281` and `:1284` (its message/hint) only; `buildUniverse` is not exported; the module's importers are `index.ts` (re-export) and `reference-integrity-suite.ts:116` (calls the rule — its output moves exactly as the rule's does, nowhere else). `validate-translatable-sections.ts` names the rule in prose only. The `extended` (rung 2b) set is unchanged; a sibling-declared target now has facts and is judged instead of skipped, which is the stricter direction.

**Checks — real exit codes, this review's worktree at head `1ea01b6649`, deps built (`pnpm --filter '@objectstack/lint^...' build` exit 0, then `@objectstack/lint` build exit 0):** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint test` **0** (106 files, 4000 passed / 5 skipped) · `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint typecheck` **0** (incl. `check:test-typecheck`) · the changed test file alone, verbose: 105/105, exit **0**, the nine #19064 cases listed by name · `eslint --no-inline-config` on the two changed source files **0** · the 57 gate families `dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derives for these three paths, run one by one with `origin/main` read as `2277d1fcd1` at run start: **54 exited 0**; the other three exited **3**, which each gate's own text defines as "NOT MEASURED — nothing was measured" for want of a whole-repo `pnpm build` (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:type-check-debt`); each exit code was captured before any pipe. Those three are declared to CI's `Lint & Repo Gates` / `Type Check · debt ledger` (the latter read `success` on this head).

**NOT MEASURED, and why:** whole-repo `pnpm lint` (only the two changed files were linted here; CI's `Lint & Repo Gates` was `in_progress` on this head when read — every other required context read `success`, observed as check-run status, not re-derived) · an end-to-end `os build` on a real fixture: `examples/app-multi-package` declares no `translations` at all (`git grep -l translations 2277d1fcd1 -- examples/app-multi-package/` prints nothing; lit control on `examples/app-crm/` prints 3 files), so no shipped fixture exhibits this defect and every reading above is on the probe shape · the runtime resolution claim was read off `memory-i18n.ts`, not booted.

**Dev flags and out-of-scope findings, answered:** `open_questions` — none. (1) the same false orphan on this rule's `dashboards` / `flows` / `globalActions` rungs — consistent with what I measured on `main` (`buildUniverse` reads those collections at top level only, `:1050`, `:1081`, `:964`); not this PR's scope, a real card. (2) the 40-rule structural survey — noted, not verified. (3) `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx:1016` still reads "`objects.{object}` — an object this stack defines, or a platform object" — confirmed on `2277d1fcd1`; it now understates two rungs; a doc nit for the next rung card. One nit of my own, not blocking: the new docblock's sentence "this file's header already declared that reach for this rung" (head `:858-:859`, echoed in the PR body and changeset) overstates — the pre-PR header's ladder said "own object" only; the reach was declared in the nav helper's docblock for the contribution carriers. The PR's own header edit makes the header say it now, so the sentence is true of the tree after landing and misattributes only the past.

**Governance:** file list is `.changeset/…`, `packages/lint/src/…` (2) — no governed surface; draft, no label or body touched by this review.

Independence pair —
(a) Measured first-hand: the two greps and their lit control on `2277d1fcd1`; the blob identity of the rule file across `74fb2f7a80` / `2277d1fcd1` / head; the probe (nine cases) on the base and head blobs through `packageBodyAsStack`'s exact shape; the verbose run of the changed test file (nine pins by name); the head test file against the base blob; the three ablations with blob hashes; the export-line diff; the read sites of `universe.objects` and both value maps; the importers; `packageBodyAsStack` / `artifactPackages` shapes; the i18n merge seam; the fixture grep; every exit code listed above; the pre-record `--pair 19347` reading.
(b) Taken from someone else's reading and NOT verified: CI check-run conclusions (status only); the dev's `dispatch-gates --ran` tally and its `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` run (superseded by my own above, not confirmed line-for-line); the dev's structural survey of 40 other rules; that #19060 landed as `6f8d751bc1` (read as a subject line in `git log`, its content not re-diffed).
